title: EU says COP31 draft could make talks 'untenable' as fight over IPCC report deepens
dek: With three days left in Antalya, Europe wants big changes to the first draft deal, a European official criticised a bloc including India and Saudi Arabia, and the summit's negotiator promises at least one more text.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
The European Union's climate envoy, Wopke Hoekstra, said on Tuesday that the first draft of the main decision at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, "does not go in the right direction and needs significant change", and warned that it could make the negotiations "untenable", according to reports. Australia's climate minister, Chris Bowen, who is steering the talks as President of Negotiations, said there would be "at least one more draft" before the summit's scheduled close on Friday, 20 November.

An unnamed European official singled out a negotiating bloc whose members include Saudi Arabia and India, saying of its positions: "These things are obviously unacceptable," according to reports. India has said it will not accept new obligations on developing countries.

## What is in dispute

The 18-page "cover decision" published on Monday calls for "accelerated action to phase out fossil fuels", asks developed countries to aim for net zero emissions by 2030, and says adaptation finance should be tripled to at least $120 billion. The summit presidency said in a note with the text that the draft "is not intended to reflect consensus" but to support further talks, adding that it contained elements "proposed by some Parties that other Parties have indicated they do not support". Any final outcome, it said, "will need to reflect the consensus of Parties".

A second fight is over the timing of the seventh assessment report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), the UN's scientific review of climate change. Dozens of European, African and Pacific countries want it published before the next review of global climate efforts, known as the global stocktake, at COP33 in 2028. The IPCC suspended its last meeting without agreement, and a new session is due in December, according to reports. Saudi Arabia's delegation said on Tuesday that the kingdom "is not seeking to delay climate science" and favoured "publication timelines that allow sufficient scientific review, transparency and meaningful participation", without saying when the reports should come out.

Ilana Seid, who chairs the Alliance of Small Island States, called the delays "unjustifiable", and Antigua and Barbuda's environment minister, Michael Joseph, said a consensus on net zero "might be very, very difficult", according to reports.

## India's position

Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav told a high-level ministerial round table on a "just transition" on Monday that there was no one-size-fits-all approach, and called for finance, technology transfer and capacity-building for developing countries, according to reports. He backed a "two-tier, Party-guided" mechanism for a just transition. India has also declined to join a pledge on electrification launched at the summit, according to reports.

India's position rests on the principle, written into the UN climate convention, that rich countries, which are responsible for most past emissions, should cut faster and pay for developing countries' transition. India relies on coal for most of its electricity and has a target of net zero by 2070.

## What happens next

Negotiators are working on a revised cover decision. UN climate summits frequently run beyond their scheduled end, because every decision needs consensus among nearly 200 countries.
